claims.statement: Per-block linear concept vectors extracted by RFM from Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct residual-stream activations, added additively at inference, steer the model toward or away from a target concept — beating both an unsteered baseline and a matched-random-direction control on the anti-refusal, political-stance, and honesty demo scenarios.

data.source: refusal (AdvBench harmful+response pairs, n=521); political-stance (DMX-generated gpt-5.4 paired, n=400); honesty (TruthfulQA + local honesty pairs, ~800); GPT-4o-2024-11-20 as judge
data.available_n: refusal 521 / political 400 / honesty ~800 paired; 50 held-out prompts per concept
data.used_n: 400 paired (train 300 / val 100) + 50 held-out prompts per concept + 7-point alpha sweep + matched-random control at alpha=+/-3
data.subset_note: 3 concepts x 32 blocks screen; refusal auto-argmax picked block 0 (probe tied at 1.0 — trivially separable); pinned block-14 re-run also performed (B5/C1b/C1c). Follow-up high-alpha run for refusal at alpha up to +12.

claims.method: Screen 32 blocks via linear probe -> RFM (AGOP, 3-5 iterations) at chosen block -> generate at alpha in {-3..+3} plus matched-random-direction control -> GPT-4o rubric-judge 5-point steering-effect scale. Refusal follow-up sweeps alpha in {0,3,5,8,12}. Success predicate per concept: mean rubric shift > baseline AND > matched-random control at dev-selected alpha.

main_experiment.key_stats: political SUPPORTED: alpha=-3->3.08, alpha=0->3.66, alpha=+3->4.02 (Delta_range=0.94); matched-random control at alpha=+/-3 only |Delta|=0.30/0.12 (RFM 2-3x larger). honesty PARTIAL: alpha=+3 Delta=+0.14 (within judge std=1.25); random control comparable. refusal NULL: all alpha values 1.00-1.14 (saturated at 1); safety unbroken even at alpha=+12 (gibberish at alpha>=8).
main_experiment.headline: Political stance shows clean signed monotone steering with matched-random-control gap; honesty is within judge noise; refusal safety training is robust to single-direction additive steering.

claims.statement: A C++ concept vector extracted by the same RFM procedure, added at inference to Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct residuals, raises test-case pass rate on HackerRank algorithmic problems above both the default (Python) output and prompt-only 'Answer in C++.' — a functional-utility gain, not a stylistic shift.

data.source: HackerRank eval (existing /data/zhenqian/data/hackerrank, 20 problems available); extraction pairs from 53 HackerRank real + 350 DMX-synth Python/C++ snippets (400 total)
data.available_n: 20 HackerRank held-out problems (eval_set.jsonl only has 20); 400 paired snippets for extraction
data.used_n: 10 dev + 10 held-out x 2 seeds x 3 conditions; 400 paired for extraction
data.subset_note: reduced from plan's 30 held-out because eval_set.jsonl only had 20 problems (10 dev + 10 held-out); [suspected under-power: used_n 20/60, seeds 2/N/A, grid 1 alpha_star only]

claims.method: RFM on 400 paired Python/C++ snippets (screen 32 blocks, best block=19); apply alpha*v_cpp additively at inference. Baselines: (a) default Python, (b) prompt-only 'Answer in C++.', (c) alpha=+3 steered. Metric: test-case pass rate on HackerRank hidden tests. Alpha chosen on 10 dev problems.

main_experiment.key_stats: default (Python): pass=0.600, cpp_frac=0.00. cpp_prompt_only: pass=0.433, cpp_frac=1.00. cpp_steered (alpha=+3, block=19): pass=0.567, cpp_frac=0.00 — steered vector at alpha=+3 does NOT switch output language; higher alpha causes gibberish. Success predicate steered > max(default, prompt-only) fails: 0.57 < 0.60.
main_experiment.headline: C++ concept vector encodes the 'Language: X.\n' training prefix rather than intrinsic C++ syntax; alpha=+3 fails to switch output language and does not beat default Python baseline.

claims.statement: A concept vector extracted by RFM on English-only paired data steers Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct responses when prompts are asked in Chinese, French, or Spanish — same additive intervention, same vector, different-language prompt.

data.source: C1 held-out honesty prompts + GPT-4o translation into ZH/FR/ES
data.used_n: 50 x 4 = 200 cells + unsteered baseline per cell (400 total generations judged)
data.subset_note: Reuses C1 EN-trained honesty vector at block 15, alpha*=+3.0 (locked by --alpha-star since c1's argmax-|Delta| labelling picked alpha=-3)

claims.method: Apply v_honesty (block 15, alpha=+3.0) additively at inference for the same 50 prompts translated into ZH/FR/ES. GPT-4o-2024-11-20 as multilingual rubric-judge; Wilcoxon per-language significance test.

main_experiment.key_stats: EN mean_steered=4.38, mean_unsteered=4.18, shift=+0.20, p=0.23. ZH 3.76/3.44 shift=+0.32 p=0.11 (largest single-lang shift). FR 3.78/3.88 shift=-0.10 p=0.67 (reverses sign). ES 4.10/3.90 shift=+0.20 p=0.27. Direction preserved in 3 of 4 langs (2 of 3 target languages); no lang reaches p<0.05.
main_experiment.headline: Direction preserved in ZH/ES/EN with ZH the largest single-lang shift; FR reverses sign; no lang stat-significant — but honesty vector's mono-lingual signal is intrinsically small (C1 EN Delta=+0.14), so the cross-lingual noise level tracks the underlying weakness.

claims.statement: Linear combinations of >=2 RFM concept vectors enable simultaneous multi-concept steering: the combined intervention induces both target effects, not merely one.

data.source: C1 vectors + new formal_tone vector (DMX gpt-5.4 pairs, n=400) + technical_persona vector (DMX pairs, n=400); combo held-out prompts hand-crafted (20 x 2 combos)
data.used_n: 15 held-out per combo x 3 conditions (v1-only, v2-only, sum); 5 dev per combo
data.subset_note: reduced from plan's 20 held to 15 (n_dev=5 subtracted from 20-prompt file); both combos used pinned block-14 vectors from B5 re-extraction

claims.method: Two combos: (i) v_honesty(block 15, alpha=+1) + v_refusal_neg(block 14, alpha=+1); (ii) v_formal_tone + v_technical_persona (both block 14, alpha=(1,1)). Generate at v1-only, v2-only, and sum; judge each of two target effects independently with GPT-4o. Success predicate: sum's rubric on target-1 > v2-only's rubric on target-1 AND sum's rubric on target-2 > v1-only's rubric on target-2.

main_experiment.key_stats: Combo1 (honesty+refusal_neg): v1_only r1(honesty)=4.87 r2=2.47; v2_only r1=4.87 r2=2.33; sum r1=4.73 r2=2.53. sum r1 fails predicate (4.73 <= 4.87 v2_only). Combo2 (formal+technical): all at ceiling ~5.0/~4.7. Both combos' r1 saturates at v1/v2-only ceiling.
main_experiment.headline: Single-vector interventions already saturate the rubric ceiling on the tested prompt sets; the strict compositional-gain predicate is trivially unachievable — the test is uninformative here (concept-collision is minimal, so this is a measurement-ceiling failure rather than a composition failure).

claims.statement: Internal-feature classifiers (RFM concept vector <h_l, v_c> and matched linear probes at the same block) built on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct residual-stream activations detect hallucinations (HaluEval-General) and toxic content (ToxicChat) with strictly higher AUROC than GPT-4o-2024-11-20 used as a black-box output judge — despite Llama-3.1-8B being a substantially smaller model than GPT-4o.

data.source: HaluEval-General (/data/zhenqian/data/monitoring/hegen, 2000 samples 1200/400/400 split); ToxicChat (/data/zhenqian/data/monitoring/toxicchat, 584 balanced 350/116/118 split — capped at 2*min(n_pos)=584 since 1708neg/292pos); ToxicChat-T5-Large as toxicity baseline
data.used_n: HaluEval 2000 (1200 train / 400 val / 400 test); ToxicChat 584 balanced (350/116/118)
data.subset_note: ToxicChat balanced from imbalanced source (292 positives cap => 584 total)

claims.method: For each concept (hallucinated vs faithful; toxic vs non-toxic): screen 32 blocks with linear probe on train; fit RFM at each block. Score held-out by <h_l, v_c> (RFM) and by fitted probe. Compare AUROC vs (i) GPT-4o called as output judge, (ii) ToxicChat-T5-Large on ToxicChat. Success: internal AUROC > GPT-4o AUROC on both datasets.

main_experiment.key_stats: HaluEval-General (n_test=400): best-probe AUROC=0.986 (blk 11), best-RFM AUROC=0.984 (blk 13), GPT-4o=0.685 -> Delta approx +0.30. ToxicChat (n_test=118): best-probe AUROC=0.922 (blk 31), best-RFM AUROC=0.945 (blk 30), GPT-4o=0.882 -> Delta approx +0.06; ToxicChat-T5-Large=1.000 (in-distribution fine-tuned).
main_experiment.headline: Internal features from Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct outperform GPT-4o as a hallucination/toxicity monitor on both benchmarks — cleanly reproduces the 'small model internals beat large model output judge' premise.
